post.caption: Fluorescence is named after the mineral fluorite. George Stokes coined the word in 1852, from fluorspar. Its name comes from a Latin word meaning to flow. Metalmakers once used it as a flux. The element fluorine is also named after the mineral. Fluorite is soft, so it suits earrings better than rings. Traces of other elements give it nearly every color. Blue John is a banded purple and blue fluorite from Derbyshire. In Britain it comes only from two caverns near Castleton. In 1768, Matthew Boulton asked for a mine lease to make vases. Raw Blue John is dried about a year, then soaked in resin.
